input: Shadow a midwife for my doula certification hours

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number of hours required and what activities count toward certification directly shapes how long and how intensive the shadowing arrangement needs to be.
Whether the user already has a midwife contact or needs to find one entirely changes the first steps — outreach vs. coordination.
The user's deadline for completing these hours affects urgency and how many shadowing sessions need to be scheduled.
The setting (hospital, birth center, home births) determines what kind of midwife to seek and what the user will be exposed to during hours.
The certifying body's documentation requirements (forms, signatures, logs) determine what the user must prepare and bring to each shadowing session.
The user may have a preferred birth philosophy or specialty focus (e.g., high-risk, low-intervention) that should guide which midwife they approach.
Understanding what the certifying organization explicitly accepts as valid shadowing hours ensures the user's time counts and nothing needs to be repeated.

gold.taskTitle: Shadow a Midwife for Doula Certification Hours
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to arrange and complete shadowing hours with a midwife as a requirement toward earning their doula certification.

questions.title: How many shadowing hours does your certification require?
questions.description: Identify the exact number of clinical observation hours mandated by the user's specific doula certification program so the scope of the shadowing arrangement is clear.

questions.title: Do you already have a midwife willing to host you?
questions.description: Determine whether the user has an existing professional contact or needs to research, reach out to, and secure a midwife willing to take on an observer.

questions.title: When is your deadline to complete these hours?
questions.description: Establish the certification submission deadline so the plan accounts for the right level of urgency and scheduling frequency.

questions.title: What birth setting do you want to shadow in?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user prefers a hospital, accredited birth center, or home birth environment, as this shapes which midwives are relevant to contact.

questions.title: What documentation must you submit to prove your hours?
questions.description: Find out what paperwork, signatures, or observation logs the certifying body requires so the user arrives at each session fully prepared to capture valid records.

questions.title: Is there a birth philosophy or specialty you want to focus on?
questions.description: Determine whether the user has a preference such as low-intervention, midwifery model of care, or a specific population so the right midwife match can be prioritized.

questions.title: Does your certifying body specify what qualifies as valid shadowing?
questions.description: Check whether the program has explicit rules about what types of births, procedures, or activities count toward hours to ensure nothing the user observes is disqualified.
